claim: TNBC constitutes 15-20% of breast cancers with the highest mortality among all breast cancer subtypes.
source: Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) is characterized by absence of hormone receptor and human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2) amplification, which constitutes 15–20% of breast cancers with the highest mortality among all breast cancer subtypes (Arroyo-Crespo et al., 2019; Kim et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published literature (Arroyo-Crespo et al., 2019; Kim et al., 2018).

claim: Targeted therapy towards TNBC still lacks and conventional chemotherapy remains the standard care for TNBC patients.
source: In contrast to hormone receptor positive breast cancer (luminal subtype), targeted therapy towards TNBC still lacks and conventional chemotherapy remains the standard care for TNBC patients (Wahba and El-Hadaad, 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to published literature (Wahba and El-Hadaad, 2015).

claim: PARP inhibitors for BRCA-1 mutated breast cancer have been approved by FDA.
source: TNBC targeted therapies have been actively developed and approved by FDA, including PARP inhibitors for BRCA-1 mutated breast cancer, perbrolizumab-based immunotherapy, and Sacituzumab for Trop-2 (Vagia et al., 2020)
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to published literature (Vagia et al., 2020).

claim: Pembrolizumab-based immunotherapy has been approved by FDA for TNBC.
source: TNBC targeted therapies have been actively developed and approved by FDA, including PARP inhibitors for BRCA-1 mutated breast cancer, perbrolizumab-based immunotherapy, and Sacituzumab for Trop-2 (Vagia et al., 2020)
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to published literature (Vagia et al., 2020).

claim: Sacituzumab for Trop-2 has been approved by FDA for TNBC.
source: TNBC targeted therapies have been actively developed and approved by FDA, including PARP inhibitors for BRCA-1 mutated breast cancer, perbrolizumab-based immunotherapy, and Sacituzumab for Trop-2 (Vagia et al., 2020)
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to published literature (Vagia et al., 2020).

claim: EMT induces epithelial cells to acquire mesenchymal phenotypes, resulting in tumour progression and metastasis.
source: Epithelial-mesenchymal transformation (EMT) induces epithelial cells to acquire mesenchymal phenotypes, resulting in tumour progression and metastasis (Sikandar et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to published literature (Sikandar et al., 2017).

claim: Progression of EMT is critical for aggression of TNBC.
source: Previous studies have proven that progression of EMT is critical for aggression of TNBC (Xu et al., 2012; Zhao et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published literature (Xu et al., 2012; Zhao et al., 2014).

claim: Invasive cancer cells adhere to extracellular molecules and disrupt the extracellular matrix to initiate the metastatic process.
source: It is well known that invasive cancer cells adhere to extracellular molecules and disrupt the extracellular matrix (ECM) to initiate the metastatic process (Ishaque et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to published literature (Ishaque et al., 2018) and draws on established scientific knowledge.

claim: TLNs are cytoplasmic adapter proteins essential for integrin-mediated cell adhesion to the ECM.
source: TLNs are cytoplasmic adapter proteins essential for integrin-mediated cell adhesion to the ECM.
evidence: The claim draws on established scientific knowledge about TLN function.

claim: TLNs are responsible for the activation of integrins via linking integrins to cytoskeletal actin and coordinating recruitment of microtubules to adhesion sites.
source: Moreover, TLNs are responsible for the activation of integrins via linking integrins to cytoskeletal actin and coordinating recruitment of microtubules to adhesion sites (Gough and Goult, 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to published literature (Gough and Goult, 2018).

claim: Loss of TLNs can impair EMT and the acquisition of cell motility.
source: Loss of TLNs can impair EMT and the acquisition of cell motility (Thapa et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to published literature (Thapa et al., 2017).

claim: There are two isoforms of TLNs: TLN1 and TLN2.
source: There are two isoforms of TLNs: TLN1 and TLN2 (Gough and Goult, 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to published literature (Gough and Goult, 2018).

claim: TLN1 is expressed in almost all tissues.
source: TLN1 is expressed in almost all tissues, while TLN2 is usually expressed mainly in the heart, brain, testis, and muscle (Debrand et al., 2009; Manso et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published literature (Debrand et al., 2009; Manso et al., 2013).

claim: TLN2 is usually expressed mainly in the heart, brain, testis, and muscle.
source: TLN1 is expressed in almost all tissues, while TLN2 is usually expressed mainly in the heart, brain, testis, and muscle (Debrand et al., 2009; Manso et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published literature (Debrand et al., 2009; Manso et al., 2013).

claim: TLN1 is located in focal adhesion and regulates integrin signalling and promotes metastasis in different cancers.
source: TLN1 is located in focal adhesion (FA), which regulates integrin signalling and promotes metastasis in different cancers (Desiniotis and Kyprianou, 2011; Hoshino et al., 2015; Klapholz and Brown, 2017; Seguin et al., 2015), including prostate cancer (Jin et al., 2015), colon cancer (Bostanci et al., 2014), and oral squamous cell carcinoma (Lai et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to published literature (Desiniotis and Kyprianou, 2011; Hoshino et al., 2015; Klapholz and Brown, 2017; Seguin et al., 2015; Jin et al., 2015; Bostanci et al., 2014; Lai et al., 2011).

claim: The auto-inhibition of TLN1 controls cell-ECM adhesion, migration, and wound healing in vivo.
source: Recent studies have reported that the auto-inhibition of TLN1 controls cell-ECM (CEM) adhesion, migration, and wound healing in vivo (Haage et al., 2018)
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to published literature (Haage et al., 2018).

claim: Disrupting the auto-inhibition of TLN1 leads to more mature and stable FAs.
source: and disrupting this auto-inhibition leads to more mature and stable FAs (Haage et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to published literature (Haage et al., 2018).

claim: The rapid transition between the active and inactive conformations of TLN1 regulates FA turnover.
source: Other studies have also shown that the rapid transition between the active and inactive conformations of TLN1 regulates FA turnover, a critical process for cell adhesion and signal transduction (Dedden et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to published literature (Dedden et al., 2019).

claim: Higher TLN1 transcripts are found in TNBC than in other clinical breast cancer subtypes.
source: Moreover, a previous study found higher TLN1 transcripts in TNBC than in other clinical breast cancer subtypes (Singel et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to published literature (Singel et al., 2013).

claim: A total of 171 patients with TNBC were recruited at Shengjing Hospital of China Medical University.
source: A total of 171 patients with TNBC were recruited at Shengjing Hospital of China Medical University.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the manuscript describing the patient cohort.

claim: There was no correlation between integrin family members and different breast cancer types using TCGA database.
source: However, we found no correlation between integrin family members and different breast cancer types using TCGA database (Figure 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by data analysis from TCGA database and presented in Figure 1A.

claim: TLN1 may play an important role in breast cancer, especially in TNBC.
source: Correlation between TLN1 and the integrin family in different types of the TCGA-BRCA dataset from TIMER database showed that TLN1 may play an important role in breast cancer, especially in TNBC (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A-B).
evidence: The claim is based on data analysis from TIMER database and presented in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A-B.

claim: TLN1 was ubiquitously expressed in the membrane and cytoplasm of paraneoplastic and tumour tissues.
source: Immunohistochemistry of TLN1 showed that TLN1 was ubiquitously expressed in the membrane and cytoplasm of paraneoplastic and tumour tissues (Figure 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data presented in Figure 1B.

claim: The relative protein levels of TLN1 in TNBC tumour tissues were significantly higher than those in para-cancerous breast tissues.
source: Western blotting of freshly dissected TNBC tumours revealed that the relative protein levels of TLN1 in TNBC tumour tissues were significantly higher than those in para-cancerous breast tissues (Figure 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by western blotting data presented in Figure 1C.

claim: TLN1 was highly expressed in 43.9% of TNBCs.
source: Statistical analysis shows that TLN1 was highly expressed in 43.9% of TNBCs
evidence: The claim is based on statistical analysis of the patient cohort data.

claim: Higher expression of TLN1 was significantly associated with shorter DFS in TNBCs (HR = 3.19, p < 0.001).
source: and the DFS of high and low expression of TLN1 shows higher expression of TLN1 was significantly associated with shorter DFS in TNBCs (HR = 3.19, p < 0.001, Figure 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by survival analysis data presented in Figure 1D.

claim: High level of TLN1 expression was significantly associated with T3-T4 stage (p = 0.03).
source: Stratified analysis indicated that high level of TLN1 expression were significantly associated with T3-T4 stage (p = 0.03), positive lymph node metastasis (p < 0.001), and high Ki67 index (p < 0.001) in all 171 TNBCs (Figure 1E).
evidence: The claim is supported by stratified analysis data presented in Figure 1E.

claim: High level of TLN1 expression was significantly associated with positive lymph node metastasis (p < 0.001).
source: Stratified analysis indicated that high level of TLN1 expression were significantly associated with T3-T4 stage (p = 0.03), positive lymph node metastasis (p < 0.001), and high Ki67 index (p < 0.001) in all 171 TNBCs (Figure 1E).
evidence: The claim is supported by stratified analysis data presented in Figure 1E.

claim: High level of TLN1 expression was significantly associated with high Ki67 index (p < 0.001).
source: Stratified analysis indicated that high level of TLN1 expression were significantly associated with T3-T4 stage (p = 0.03), positive lymph node metastasis (p < 0.001), and high Ki67 index (p < 0.001) in all 171 TNBCs (Figure 1E).
evidence: The claim is supported by stratified analysis data presented in Figure 1E.

claim: High expression of TLN1 was detected in chest wall recurrence, lymphatic metastasis, and intestinal metastasis.
source: Besides, high expression of TLN1 was detected in chest wall recurrence, lymphatic metastasis, and intestinal metastasis (Figure 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data presented in Figure 1B.

claim: TLN1 upregulation was associated with poor prognosis in TNBC patients.
source: Hence, TLN1 upregulation was associated with poor prognosis in TNBC patients.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the survival and clinical correlation data presented earlier.

claim: TLN2 shares 76% protein sequence identity with TLN1.
source: Considering that TLN2 shares 76% protein sequence identity with TLN1 (Gough and Goult, 2018)
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to published literature (Gough and Goult, 2018).

claim: TLN2 mRNA in breast cancer tissue were significantly lower than in normal breast tissues (p < 0.01).
source: Results showed that TLN2 mRNA in breast cancer tissue were significantly lower than in normal breast tissues (p < 0.01)
evidence: The claim is based on analysis of TCGA database data.

claim: There was no difference in TLN2 levels between luminal and TNBC subtypes.
source: and there was no difference in levels between luminal and TNBC, HER2+ and TNBC subtypes, except for the comparison between luminal and HER2+ subtypes (p = 0.006) (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: The claim is based on analysis of TCGA database data presented in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C.

claim: There was no significant difference in survival between high and low expression of TLN2 within each subtype of breast cancer.
source: Also, there was no significant difference in survival between high and low expression of TLN2 within each subtype of breast cancer (Figure 1—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: The claim is based on survival analysis data presented in Figure 1—figure supplement 1D.

claim: The TNBC cell lines MDA-MB-231 and BT-549 showed much higher levels of TLN1 than luminal cell line MCF-7 and HER2+ cell line SK-BR-3 cells.
source: The TNBC cell lines MDA-MB-231 and BT-549 showed much higher levels of TLN1 than luminal cell line MCF-7 and HER2+ cell line SK-BR-3 cells (Figure 2A).
evidence: The claim is supported by western blot data presented in Figure 2A.

claim: Silencing TLN1 significantly inhibited the proliferation of MDA-MB-231 cells.
source: Silencing TLN1 significantly inhibited the proliferation of MDA-MB-231 cells (Figure 2C)
evidence: The claim is supported by EdU assay data presented in Figure 2C.

claim: Silencing TLN1 increased the frequency of spontaneous apoptosis in MDA-MB-231 cells.
source: and increased the frequency of spontaneous apoptosis (Figure 2D)
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data presented in Figure 2D.

claim: Silencing TLN1 increased the number of apoptosis-related vacuoles in MDA-MB-231 cells.
source: and the number of apoptosis-related vacuoles in MDA-MB-231 cells (Figure 2E).
evidence: The claim is supported by transmission electron microscopy data presented in Figure 2E.

claim: Silencing TLN1 showed significant reduction of tumour size and weight in NOD/SCID mice implanted with MDA-MB-231 cells.
source: More importantly, silencing TLN1 was shown significant reduction of tumour size and weight in NOD/SCID mice implanted with 106 MDA-MB-231/NC or shTLN1 cells in the mammary fat pad (Figure 2F).
evidence: The claim is supported by xenograft data presented in Figure 2F.

claim: Silencing TLN1 can inhibit the growth of TNBC cells in vitro and in vivo.
source: Together, these data demonstrate that silencing TLN1 can inhibit the growth of TNBC cells in vitro and in vivo.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the proliferation, apoptosis, and xenograft data presented.

claim: Silencing TLN1 significantly inhibited the cell adhesion, migration, and invasion of MDA-MB-231 cells.
source: We found that silencing TLN1 significantly inhibited the cell adhesion, migration, and invasion of MDA-MB-231 cells (Figure 3A and B)
evidence: The claim is supported by adhesion and transwell assay data presented in Figure 3A and B.

claim: Silencing TLN1 significantly inhibited the cell adhesion, migration, and invasion of BT549 cells.
source: and BT549 cells (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A-C).
evidence: The claim is supported by data presented in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A-C.

claim: Silencing TLN1 significantly increased the expression of CK18 and E-cadherin in MDA-MB-231 cells.
source: Additionally, silencing TLN1 significantly increased the expression of CK18 and E-cadherin but significantly decreased the expression of N-cadherin and vimentin in MDA-MB-231 cells
evidence: The claim is supported by western blot data presented in Figure 3C and D.

claim: Silencing TLN1 significantly decreased the expression of N-cadherin and vimentin in MDA-MB-231 cells.
source: Additionally, silencing TLN1 significantly increased the expression of CK18 and E-cadherin but significantly decreased the expression of N-cadherin and vimentin in MDA-MB-231 cells
evidence: The claim is supported by western blot data presented in Figure 3C and D.

claim: Silencing TLN1 inhibited EMT in TNBC cells.
source: suggesting that silencing TLN1 inhibited EMT in TNBC cells (Figure 3C and D).
evidence: The claim is inferred from the changes in EMT markers (E-cadherin, N-cadherin, vimentin) shown in Figure 3C and D.

claim: Silencing TLN1 suppressed lung metastasis in vivo.
source: More importantly, silencing TLN1 suppressed lung metastasis in vivo, as demonstrated by significant decreases in the number and size of lung metastatic nodules in mice injected with shTLN1 cells (Figure 3E).
evidence: The claim is supported by lung metastasis data presented in Figure 3E.

claim: Overexpression of integrin β1 could rescue invasion, migration, and adhesion in shTLN1 cells.
source: While overexpression of integrin β1 could rescue invasion, migration, and adhesion in shTLN1 cells (Figure 3F–H).
evidence: The claim is supported by rescue experiment data presented in Figure 3F–H.

claim: Silencing TLN1 may inhibit TNBC cell adhesion and metastasis by attenuating EMT.
source: Thus, silencing TLN1 may inhibit TNBC cell adhesion and metastasis by attenuating EMT.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the EMT marker changes and functional assay results.

claim: There were 156 DEPs between MDA-MB-231/NC and shTLN1 cells; 76 were upregulated, whereas 80 were downregulated.
source: There were 156 DEPs between these cells; 76 were upregulated, whereas 80 were downregulated (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: The claim is supported by TMT proteomics data presented in Figure 3—figure supplement 2A.

claim: TLN1-related DEPs were involved in tissue development, positive regulation of cell migration, microtubule organization, cell differentiation, and protein-binding activity.
source: The results of Gene Ontology (GO) functional enrichment analysis of DEPs indicated that these TLN1-related DEPs were involved in tissue development, positive regulation of cell migration, microtubule organization, cell differentiation, and protein-binding activity (Figure 3—figure supplement 2B, C, D).
evidence: The claim is supported by GO enrichment analysis data presented in Figure 3—figure supplement 2B, C, D.

claim: Mutations within both integrins β1 and β3 may abolish TLN binding and decrease integrin affinity.
source: Given that mutations within both integrins β1 (Bouaouina et al., 2008) and β3 (Tadokoro et al., 2003) may abolish TLN binding and decrease integrin affinity
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published literature (Bouaouina et al., 2008; Tadokoro et al., 2003).

claim: TLN1 ablation universally leads to integrin adhesion defects.
source: TLN1 ablation universally leads to integrin adhesion defects (Chen et al., 2017; Jin et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published literature (Chen et al., 2017; Jin et al., 2015).

claim: There was a significant interaction between TLN1 and integrin β1 in MDA-MB-231 cells.
source: Firstly, we validated the interactions between TLN1 and integrin β1 or β3 in MDA-MB-231 cells by immunoprecipitation and found that there was a significant interaction between TLN1 and integrin β1 but not between TLN1 and integrin β3, though a non-specific band was seen in the TLN1 pull-down of integrin β3, which was probably a trace left by electrophoresis (Figure 4A).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunoprecipitation data presented in Figure 4A.

claim: There was no significant interaction between TLN1 and integrin β3 in MDA-MB-231 cells.
source: Firstly, we validated the interactions between TLN1 and integrin β1 or β3 in MDA-MB-231 cells by immunoprecipitation and found that there was a significant interaction between TLN1 and integrin β1 but not between TLN1 and integrin β3, though a non-specific band was seen in the TLN1 pull-down of integrin β3, which was probably a trace left by electrophoresis (Figure 4A).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunoprecipitation data presented in Figure 4A.

claim: TLN1 and integrin β1 were scattered in the cytoplasm while co-located in FAs at both poles of the cell.
source: Subsequently, immunofluorescence showed that TLN1 and integrin β1 were scattered in the cytoplasm while co-located in FAs at both poles of the cell (Figure 4B).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data presented in Figure 4B.

claim: Silencing TLN1 led to significantly shorter cells, fewer FAs, the predominant localization of FAs on the cell membrane, and significant thickening of the actin cortex.
source: Results showed that silencing TLN1 led to significantly shorter cells, fewer FAs, the predominant localization of FAs on the cell membrane, and significant thickening of the actin cortex (Figure 4C).
evidence: The claim is supported by confocal microscopy data presented in Figure 4C.

claim: The morphology of shTLN1 cells was no longer as fusiform as MDA-MB-231/NC cells.
source: Moreover, light microscopic imaging showed that the morphology of shTLN1 cells was no longer as fusiform as MDA-MB-231/NC cells (Figure 4D).
evidence: The claim is supported by light microscopy data presented in Figure 4D.

claim: Silencing TLN1 in MDA-MB-231 cells reduced the relative levels of integrin β1, as well as the levels of phosphorylated AKT and FAK.
source: Western blot analysis further indicated that silencing TLN1 in MDA-MB-231 cells reduced the relative levels of integrin β1, as well as the levels of phosphorylated AKT and FAK (Figure 4E).
evidence: The claim is supported by western blot data presented in Figure 4E.

claim: Silencing TLN1 attenuates integrin β1 signalling in TNBC cells, which results in impaired dynamic formation and maturation of FAs.
source: These data indicate that silencing TLN1 attenuates integrin β1 signalling in TNBC cells, which results in impaired dynamic formation and maturation of FAs.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the western blot and microscopy data showing reduced integrin β1 signaling and altered FA formation.

claim: The TLN1 'head' is comprised largely of an FERM domain, which contains F0, F1, F2, and F3 domains.
source: Structurally, the TLN1 'head' is comprised largely of an FERM domain, which contains F0, F1, F2, and F3 domains (band 4.1, ezrin, radixin, and moesin) (PDB ID: 3IVF) (Goult et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to published literature (Goult et al., 2013) and structural data (PDB ID: 3IVF).

claim: The S1 and S2 chains of the PTB F3 domain are crucial for integrin binding and activation.
source: As the S1 and S2 chains of the PTB F3 domain are crucial for integrin binding and activation, the F3 domain of TLN1 was targeted (Figure 5A).
evidence: The claim draws on established structural knowledge about TLN1-integrin interactions.

claim: C67399 could obviously inhibit the cell viability of MDA-MB-231 cells.
source: The results showed that C67399 (C38H48O5, 584.79 Da, 4903–2135, Chemdiv Compond, San Diego, CA) could obviously inhibit the cell viability of MDA-MB-231 cells (Figure 5—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by cell viability assay data presented in Figure 5—figure supplement 1C.

claim: C67399 could stably bound TLN1 with a low dissociation equilibrium.
source: We also found that C67399 could stably bound TLN1 with a low dissociation equilibrium (Figure 5B).
evidence: The claim is supported by computational docking data presented in Figure 5B.

claim: C67399 interacts with Thr354, Ala389, Gln390, Ala393, Ile396, Asp397, and Ile398, in addition to Trp359, in the hydrophobic pocket of the F3 domain of TLN1.
source: Further MD simulations revealed that C67399 interacts with Thr354, Ala389, Gln390, Ala393, Ile396, Asp397, and Ile398, in addition to Trp359, in the hydrophobic pocket of the F3 domain of TLN1 (Figure 5C).
evidence: The claim is supported by molecular dynamics simulation data presented in Figure 5C.

claim: The addition of C67399 reduces the energy expenditure between TLN1 and integrin β1.
source: Moreover, the total interaction energy spectrum shows that the addition of C67399 reduces the energy expenditure between TLN1 and integrin β1 (Figure 5D).
evidence: The claim is supported by energy spectrum data from molecular dynamics simulations presented in Figure 5D.

claim: Small-molecule C67399 could block the combination of TLN1 and integrin β1 from the point of view of protein structure and in silico modelling.
source: These findings indicated that small-molecule C67399 could block the combination of TLN1 and integrin β1 from the point of view of protein structure and in silico modelling.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the computational modeling and simulation data.

claim: The IC50 of C67399 in MDA-MB-231 cells was 2.0 µM.
source: Dose-response curve for C67399 in MDA-MB-231 cells revealed that the half maximal inhibitory concentration (IC50) of C67399 was 2.0 µM (Figure 5E).
evidence: The claim is supported by dose-response curve data presented in Figure 5E.

claim: Treatment with C67399 significantly decreased the viability, adhesion, migration, and invasion of MDA-MB-231 cells and BT549 cells.
source: Functionally, treatment with C67399 significantly decreased the viability, adhesion, migration, and invasion of MDA-MB-231 cells and BT549 cells (Figure 5F, G and H and Figure 5—figure supplement 1D-E).
evidence: The claim is supported by functional assay data presented in Figure 5F, G, H and Figure 5—figure supplement 1D-E.

claim: 2.0 µM C67399 significantly reduced the expression of integrin β1, AKT, FAK, and phosphorylated FAK in MDA-MB-231 cells.
source: More importantly, 2.0 µM C67399 significantly reduced the expression of integrin β1, AKT, FAK, and phosphorylated FAK in MDA-MB-231 cells, while did not affect the expression of integrin β3 (Figure 5I).
evidence: The claim is supported by western blot data presented in Figure 5I.

claim: C67399 did not affect the expression of integrin β3 in MDA-MB-231 cells.
source: More importantly, 2.0 µM C67399 significantly reduced the expression of integrin β1, AKT, FAK, and phosphorylated FAK in MDA-MB-231 cells, while did not affect the expression of integrin β3 (Figure 5I).
evidence: The claim is supported by western blot data presented in Figure 5I.

claim: C67399 inhibited the binding of TLN1 to integrin β1 in MDA-MB-231 cells.
source: Additionally, immunoprecipitation results revealed that C67399 inhibited the binding of TLN1 to integrin β1 in MDA-MB-231 cells (Figure 5J).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunoprecipitation data presented in Figure 5J.

claim: Targeting TLN1 with C67399 suppresses TNBC cell malignancy in vitro.
source: Our findings suggest that targeting TLN1 with C67399 suppresses TNBC cell malignancy in vitro.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the functional assay and western blot data showing C67399 effects.

claim: Mice that received intravenous administration of 1.75 mg/kg C67399 twice per week showed significant reductions in the tumour volume.
source: Mice that received intravenous administration of 1.75 mg/kg C67399 twice per week showed significant reductions in the tumour volume (Figure 6A and B)
evidence: The claim is supported by xenograft tumor volume data presented in Figure 6A and B.

claim: C67399 treatment decreased the number and size of lung metastatic nodules in mice.
source: the number, and size of lung metastatic nodules (Figure 6C, D and E), indicating decreased tumour growth and attenuated lung metastasis of implanted shTLN1 cells.
evidence: The claim is supported by lung metastasis data presented in Figure 6C, D and E.

claim: A decreased proliferation index of Ki67 was observed in the C67399-treated xenograft tumours compared to the untreated MDA-MB-231 tumours.
source: Furthermore, a decreased proliferation index of Ki67 was observed in the C67399-treated xenograft tumours using immunohistochemistry, compared to the untreated MDA-MB-231 tumours (Figure 6F).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data presented in Figure 6F.

claim: No toxic reactions were observed in organs from mice treated with 1.75 mg/kg C67399 twice per week for 3 weeks.
source: We also performed H&E staining of other organs harvested from the mice treated with C67399, and no structural changes suggestive of toxicity were observed in the heart, liver, spleen, lungs, kidneys, or other organs (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A)
evidence: The claim is supported by H&E staining data presented in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A.

claim: There were no significant differences in Alcian blue staining of intestine, alanine aminotransferase, and aspartate aminotransferase activities in mice serum and blood cell counts between DMSO and C67399 groups.
source: as well as no significant differences in Alcian blue staining of intestine, alanine aminotransferase, and aspartate aminotransferase activities in mice serum and blood cell counts (Figure 6—figure supplement 1B-D).
evidence: The claim is supported by toxicity assessment data presented in Figure 6—figure supplement 1B-D.

claim: C67399 could inhibit the tumour growth and metastasis of MDA-MB-231 cells in vivo, without causing obvious structural toxic changes.
source: These results suggested that C67399 could inhibit the tumour growth and metastasis of MDA-MB-231 cells in vivo, without causing obvious structural toxic changes.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the xenograft efficacy and toxicity data.

claim: TLN1 can bind and activate integrin β1 in TNBC cells.
source: Collectively, our findings indicated that TLN1 can bind and activate integrin β1 in TNBC cells.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the immunoprecipitation and functional data presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: TLN1 can regulate the dynamic formation and maturation of FAs.
source: On the one hand, it can regulate the dynamic formation and maturation of FAs, induce EMT to promote tumour metastasis
evidence: The claim is inferred from the microscopy and functional data showing FA changes upon TLN1 silencing.

claim: TLN1 induces EMT to promote tumour metastasis.
source: On the one hand, it can regulate the dynamic formation and maturation of FAs, induce EMT to promote tumour metastasis
evidence: The claim is inferred from the EMT marker changes and metastasis data.

claim: TLN1 facilitates tumour growth by inhibiting apoptosis.
source: on the other hand, it facilitates tumour growth by inhibiting apoptosis.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the apoptosis and proliferation data showing increased apoptosis upon TLN1 silencing.

claim: C67399 can inhibit the binding of TLN1 to integrin β1.
source: Fortunately, C67399 can inhibit the binding of TLN1 to integrin β1, as well as a series of integrin β1-related pathways, and ultimately inhibit the malignancy of TNBC (Figure 6G).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunoprecipitation and functional data showing C67399 effects.

claim: C67399 can inhibit a series of integrin β1-related pathways.
source: Fortunately, C67399 can inhibit the binding of TLN1 to integrin β1, as well as a series of integrin β1-related pathways, and ultimately inhibit the malignancy of TNBC (Figure 6G).
evidence: The claim is supported by western blot data showing reduced FAK and AKT phosphorylation.

claim: C67399 can ultimately inhibit the malignancy of TNBC.
source: Fortunately, C67399 can inhibit the binding of TLN1 to integrin β1, as well as a series of integrin β1-related pathways, and ultimately inhibit the malignancy of TNBC (Figure 6G).
evidence: The claim is inferred from the in vitro and in vivo efficacy data for C67399.

claim: Loss of TLN1 function significantly enhances chemosensitivity in TNBC cell lines, but not in hormone positive cell lines.
source: Loss of TLN1 function was reported to significantly enhance chemosensitivity in TNBC cell lines, but not in hormone positive cell lines (Singel et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to published literature (Singel et al., 2013).

claim: TLN1 is a regulator of response to docetaxel and a potential therapeutic target for TNBC, but not in other types of breast cancer.
source: They concluded that TLN1 is a regulator of response to docetaxel and a potential therapeutic target for TNBC, but not in other types of breast cancer (Singel et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to published literature (Singel et al., 2013).

claim: TLN1 has a carcinogenic effect independent of chemosensitivity in TNBC.
source: In addition to its role in chemosensitivity, we found that TLN1 has a carcinogenic effect independent of chemosensitivity in TNBC, and TLN1 initiates the growth and migration of TNBC.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the proliferation, migration, and invasion data presented in the manuscript.

claim: TLN1 initiates the growth and migration of TNBC.
source: In addition to its role in chemosensitivity, we found that TLN1 has a carcinogenic effect independent of chemosensitivity in TNBC, and TLN1 initiates the growth and migration of TNBC.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the functional assay data showing reduced growth and migration upon TLN1 silencing.

claim: High expression of TLN1 in TNBC was associated with poor prognosis and malignant behaviour, including proliferation, cell adhesion, EMT, invasion, and migration.
source: In this study, we revealed that high expression of TLN1 in TNBC was associated with poor prognosis and malignant behaviour, including proliferation, cell adhesion, EMT, invasion, and migration.
evidence: The claim summarizes the clinical and functional data presented in the manuscript.

claim: TLN1 promotes TNBC malignancy as an oncogenic gene.
source: These data indicate that TLN1 promotes TNBC malignancy as an oncogenic gene, which is in accordance with previous observations in prostate cancer, colon cancer, and oral squamous cell carcinoma (Bostanci et al., 2014; Jin et al., 2015; Lai et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is inferred from the functional data and supported by citations to similar findings in other cancers.

claim: Higher TLN1 expression could be a prognostic factor for TNBC patients.
source: Given that it is very challenging to predict survival for TNBC patients after surgical resection (Brockwell et al., 2019), our data indicated that higher TLN1 expression could be a prognostic factor for TNBC patients.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the survival analysis data showing association between TLN1 expression and DFS.

claim: TLN1 is a potential therapeutic target for TNBC.
source: Our findings also highlight that TLN1 is a potential therapeutic target for TNBC.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the functional knockdown and drug treatment data.

claim: TLN1 expression in TNBC cells is much higher than in other subtypes of breast cancer cell lines.
source: Specifically, TLN1 expression in TNBC cells is much higher than in other subtypes of breast cancer cell lines
evidence: The claim is supported by western blot data comparing TLN1 levels across cell lines.

claim: Silencing TLN1 significantly attenuated the malignancy of MDA-MB-231 cells, reducing TNBC tumour growth and lung metastasis.
source: and silencing TLN1 significantly attenuated the malignancy of MDA-MB-231 cells, reducing TNBC tumour growth and lung metastasis.
evidence: The claim is supported by xenograft and metastasis data.

claim: TLN1-related signalling is crucial for TNBC malignancy.
source: These data were consistent with previous observations (Thapa et al., 2017) and support the notion that TLN1-related signalling is crucial for TNBC malignancy.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the functional data and supported by citation to published literature (Thapa et al., 2017).

claim: Malignant TNBC cells can adhere to the ECM by activating integrins.
source: It is well known that malignant TNBC cells can adhere to the ECM by activating integrins (Bays and DeMali, 2017; Bosch-Fortea and Martín-Belmonte, 2018; Hynes, 2002; Lock et al., 2008)
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published literature and draws on established knowledge.

claim: The activation of integrin-related signalling promotes EMT and metastasis in TNBC.
source: and the activation of integrin-related signalling promotes EMT and metastasis in TNBC (Wen et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to published literature (Wen et al., 2019).

claim: The 'head' of TLN1 can bind the cytoplasmic tails of integrin β through its PTB domain, resulting in integrin β activation.
source: Major insights into TLN1 demonstrated that its 'head' can bind the cytoplasmic tails of integrin β through its PTB domain, resulting in integrin β activation (Tadokoro et al., 2003).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to published literature (Tadokoro et al., 2003).

claim: TLN1 activation links integrins to the cytoskeleton by activating FAK and Src.
source: This activation links integrins to the cytoskeleton (Critchley and Gingras, 2008) by activating FAK and Src and further promotes downstream PI3K/AKT signal transduction to promote cancer malignancy (Jin et al., 2015; Klapholz and Brown, 2017; Sun et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published literature (Critchley and Gingras, 2008; Jin et al., 2015; Klapholz and Brown, 2017; Sun et al., 2019).

claim: TLN1 activation promotes downstream PI3K/AKT signal transduction to promote cancer malignancy.
source: This activation links integrins to the cytoskeleton (Critchley and Gingras, 2008) by activating FAK and Src and further promotes downstream PI3K/AKT signal transduction to promote cancer malignancy (Jin et al., 2015; Klapholz and Brown, 2017; Sun et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published literature (Jin et al., 2015; Klapholz and Brown, 2017; Sun et al., 2019).

claim: Silencing TLN1 significantly reduces FAs dynamic formation in MDA-MB-231 cells.
source: In our results, TLN1 interacts with integrin β1 and silencing TLN1 alters many proteins expression and significantly reduces FAs dynamic formation in MDA-MB-231 cells, which is similar to observations in fibroblasts and endothelial cells (Kopp et al., 2010; Nader et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy data and citations to similar findings in other cell types (Kopp et al., 2010; Nader et al., 2016).

claim: Silencing TLN1 significantly reduces integrin β1 levels as well as the levels of phosphorylated FAK.
source: In addition, silencing TLN1 was found to significantly reduce integrin β1 levels as well as the levels of phosphorylated FAK.
evidence: The claim is supported by western blot data.

claim: The reduction in integrin might be a result of TLN1 silencing-mediated integrin degradation.
source: The reduction in integrin might be a result of TLN1 silencing-mediated integrin degradation (Chinthalapudi et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is speculative and supported by a citation to published literature (Chinthalapudi et al., 2018).

claim: TLN1 is crucial for FA dynamic formation, adhesion, and invasion in TNBC cells, as well as tumour growth and metastasis.
source: These data suggest that TLN1 is crucial for FA dynamic formation, adhesion, and invasion in TNBC cells, as well as tumour growth and metastasis.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the comprehensive functional data presented.

claim: Silencing TLN1 significantly attenuated AKT phosphorylation in MDA-MB-231 cells.
source: Additionally, silencing TLN1 significantly attenuated AKT phosphorylation in MDA-MB-231 cells, demonstrating the mitigation of TLN1/integrin β1 signalling in TNBC cells.
evidence: The claim is supported by western blot data.

claim: The actin cortex is a thin layer of filamentous actin that lies beneath the plasma membrane.
source: The actin cortex is a thin layer of filamentous actin that lies beneath the plasma membrane (Litschko et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to published literature (Litschko et al., 2019) and draws on established knowledge.

claim: During EMT, actin reorganizes from a mostly cortical arrangement into stress fibres and lamellipodia.
source: During EMT, actin reorganizes from a mostly cortical arrangement into stress fibres and lamellipodia (Chalut and Paluch, 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to published literature (Chalut and Paluch, 2016).

claim: Silencing TLN1 induces thickening of the actin cortex in TNBC cells.
source: To the best of our knowledge, this study provides the first evidence that silencing TLN1 induces thickening of the actin cortex in TNBC cells
evidence: The claim is supported by confocal microscopy data showing actin cortex changes.

claim: Thickening of the actin cortex may initiate cell surface contractile tension and result in local contractions and drive cell deformations.
source: which may initiate cell surface contractile tension and result in local contractions and drive cell deformations (Chugh et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is speculative and supported by a citation to published literature (Chugh et al., 2017).

claim: Loss of TLN1 led to actin redistribution, resulting in changes in membrane dynamics.
source: Our findings indicated that loss of TLN1 led to actin redistribution, resulting in changes in membrane dynamics, and this loss may interfere with the efficient assembly or turnover of FAs, which is required for directional migration (Garcin and Straube, 2019).
evidence: The claim is inferred from the microscopy data and supported by a citation (Garcin and Straube, 2019).

claim: Loss of TLN1 may interfere with the efficient assembly or turnover of FAs, which is required for directional migration.
source: Our findings indicated that loss of TLN1 led to actin redistribution, resulting in changes in membrane dynamics, and this loss may interfere with the efficient assembly or turnover of FAs, which is required for directional migration (Garcin and Straube, 2019).
evidence: The claim is speculative and supported by a citation to published literature (Garcin and Straube, 2019).

claim: TLN1 may regulate the dynamic formation of FAs by reducing cortical actin, and then promote cell migration in TNBC cells.
source: Therefore, TLN1 may regulate the dynamic formation of FAs by reducing cortical actin, and then promote cell migration in TNBC cells.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the actin cortex and FA formation data.

claim: C67399 is a novel small-molecule compound which blocks TLN1 binding to integrin β1.
source: In this study, for the first time, we identified a novel small-molecule compound, C67399, which blocks TLN1 binding to integrin β1, through a novel computational approach named as CSTPPI against the binding interface of TLN1 with integrin β1.
evidence: The claim is supported by computational screening and experimental validation data.

claim: The advantage of CSTPPI is that conformational ensembles of TLN1-integrin β1 interfaces were used as targets for the computational screening.
source: The advantage of this CSTPPI is that conformational ensembles of TLN1-integrin β1 interfaces were used as targets for the computational screening via our in-housed developed docking tool.
evidence: The claim describes the computational methodology used.

claim: The flexibility of protein-protein interface was given full consideration in CSTPPI to improve the accuracy.
source: Therefore, the flexibility of protein-protein interface was given full consideration in our CSTPPI to improve the accuracy.
evidence: The claim describes the computational methodology used.

claim: This is the first study of identifying small-molecule compounds by targeting dynamic protein-protein binding interface.
source: This is the first study of identifying small-molecule compounds by targeting dynamic protein-protein binding interface and this may be extended to other PPI study.
evidence: The claim asserts novelty of the computational approach.

claim: C67399 could significantly ablate the invasiveness of MDA-MB-231 cells and suppress the lung metastasis in vivo.
source: Remarkably, we found that C67399 could significantly ablate the invasiveness of MDA-MB-231 cells and suppress the lung metastasis in vivo.
evidence: The claim is supported by invasion assay and lung metastasis data.

claim: TLN1 is a promising therapeutic target and C67399 is a valuable candidate compound for TNBC intervention.
source: These novel findings suggest that TLN1 is a promising therapeutic target and C67399 is a valuable candidate compound for TNBC intervention.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the comprehensive efficacy data for C67399.

claim: C67399 is the first small-molecule inhibitor of its kind that interfere in the binding interface of TLN1 with integrin β1.
source: C67399 is the first small-molecule inhibitor of its kind that interfere in the binding interface of TLN1 with integrin β1.
evidence: The claim asserts novelty of the compound.

claim: TLN1 is significantly upregulated in TNBC cells.
source: In summary, our data suggest that TLN1 is significantly upregulated in TNBC cells
evidence: The claim summarizes the expression data presented.

claim: TLN1 interacts with integrin β1 to activate downstream signalling pathways including PI3K/AKT and FAK pathways.
source: and TLN1 interacts with integrin β1 to activate downstream signalling pathways including PI3K/AKT and FAK pathways.
evidence: The claim is supported by immunoprecipitation and western blot data.

claim: The interaction of TLN1 with integrin β1 facilitates the formation of FAs and cell adhesion.
source: Furthermore, the interaction of TLN1 with integrin β1 facilitates the formation of FAs and cell adhesion, leading to the malignancy and metastasis of TNBC by enhancing EMT.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the microscopy and functional assay data.

claim: The interaction of TLN1 with integrin β1 leads to the malignancy and metastasis of TNBC by enhancing EMT.
source: Furthermore, the interaction of TLN1 with integrin β1 facilitates the formation of FAs and cell adhesion, leading to the malignancy and metastasis of TNBC by enhancing EMT.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the EMT marker and metastasis data.

claim: TLN1 could be a valuable prognostic factor and a promising therapeutic target for TNBC.
source: Hence, TLN1 could be a valuable prognostic factor and a promising therapeutic target for TNBC.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the clinical correlation and functional data.

claim: Genetically downregulating TLN1 expression could inhibit the aggressiveness and metastasis of TNBC.
source: Moreover, we identified a small-molecule compound C67399 via computational screening and we demonstrated that genetically downregulating TLN1 expression or blocking the binding of TLN1 with integrin β1 by C67399 could inhibit the aggressiveness and metastasis of TNBC.
evidence: The claim is supported by shRNA knockdown data.

claim: Blocking the binding of TLN1 with integrin β1 by C67399 could inhibit the aggressiveness and metastasis of TNBC.
source: Moreover, we identified a small-molecule compound C67399 via computational screening and we demonstrated that genetically downregulating TLN1 expression or blocking the binding of TLN1 with integrin β1 by C67399 could inhibit the aggressiveness and metastasis of TNBC.
evidence: The claim is supported by C67399 treatment data in vitro and in vivo.

claim: Upregulation of TLN1 in TNBC samples correlates with metastasis and worse prognosis.
source: Results:Upregulation of TLN1 in TNBC samples correlates with metastasis and worse prognosis.
evidence: The claim summarizes the clinical correlation data from the patient cohort.

claim: Silencing TLN1 in TNBC cells significantly attenuated the migration of tumour cells through interfering the dynamic formation of focal adhesion with integrin β1.
source: Silencing TLN1 in TNBC cells significantly attenuated the migration of tumour cells through interfering the dynamic formation of focal adhesion with integrin β1, thus regulating FAK-AKT signal pathway and epithelial-mesenchymal transformation.
evidence: The claim is supported by migration assays and microscopy data showing FA changes.

claim: Silencing TLN1 regulates FAK-AKT signal pathway.
source: Silencing TLN1 in TNBC cells significantly attenuated the migration of tumour cells through interfering the dynamic formation of focal adhesion with integrin β1, thus regulating FAK-AKT signal pathway and epithelial-mesenchymal transformation.
evidence: The claim is supported by western blot data showing changes in FAK and AKT phosphorylation.

claim: Silencing TLN1 regulates epithelial-mesenchymal transformation.
source: Silencing TLN1 in TNBC cells significantly attenuated the migration of tumour cells through interfering the dynamic formation of focal adhesion with integrin β1, thus regulating FAK-AKT signal pathway and epithelial-mesenchymal transformation.
evidence: The claim is supported by western blot data showing changes in EMT markers.

claim: Targeting the binding between TLN1 and integrin β1 by C67399 could repress metastasis of TNBC.
source: Targeting the binding between TLN1 and integrin β1 by C67399 could repress metastasis of TNBC.
evidence: The claim is supported by lung metastasis data in mice treated with C67399.

claim: TLN1 overexpression contributes to TNBC metastasis.
source: Conclusions:TLN1 overexpression contributes to TNBC metastasis and C67399 targeting TLN1 may hold promise for TNBC treatment.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the clinical correlation and functional data.

claim: C67399 targeting TLN1 may hold promise for TNBC treatment.
source: Conclusions:TLN1 overexpression contributes to TNBC metastasis and C67399 targeting TLN1 may hold promise for TNBC treatment.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the in vitro and in vivo efficacy data for C67399.
